extracted.intended_audience: owners/applicants of industrial property, IP practitioners, patent/trademark agents, and businesses operating in Vietnam
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory provisions from the Vietnamese industrial property law covering infringement, unfair competition, provisional rights, limitations, transfer and licensing, representation, compulsory licensing, and plant variety protection. Intended to guide rights-holders, applicants, representatives and state agencies on substantive standards and procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement by using commercial indications confusing with well-known marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Using commercial indications identical with, dissimilar or unrelated to goods or services on the lists of those bearing well-known marks, if such use is likely to cause confusion as to the origin of the goods or services or misleading impression as to the relationship between users of such signs and well-known mark owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade name infringement (confusion as to business entities)
rubrics_metrics.description: All acts of using commercial indications identical with, or similar to, others’ trade names having been used earlier for the same or similar type of goods or services, that cause confusion as to business entities, establishments or activities under such trade names shall be regarded as infringements of the rights to trade names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement of protected geographical indications
rubrics_metrics.description: The following acts shall be regarded as infringements of the rights to protected geographical indications: (a) Using protected geographical indications for products which do not satisfy the criteria of peculiar characteristics and quality of products bearing geographical indications although such products originate from geographical areas bearing such geographical indications; (b) Using protected geographical indications for products similar to products bearing geographical indications for the purposes of taking advantage of their reputation and popularity; (c) Using any sign identical with, or similar to, protected geographical indications for products not originating from geographical areas bearing such geographical indications and therefore misleading consumers as to that products originate from such geographical areas; (d) Using protected geographical indications of wines or spirits for wines or spirits not originating from geographical areas bearing such geographical indication, even where the true origin of goods is indicated or geographical indications are used in the form of translations or transcriptions, or accompanied by such words as 'category,' 'model,' 'type,' 'imitation' or the like.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts of unfair competition (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following acts shall be regarded as acts of unfair competition: (a) Using commercial indications to cause confusion as to business entities, business activities or commercial origin of goods or services; (b) Using commercial indications to cause confusion as to the origin, production method, utilities, quality, quantity or other characteristics of goods or services; or as to the conditions for provision of goods or services; (c) Using marks protected in a country which is a contracting party to a treaty to which the Socialist Republic of Vietnam is also a contracting party and under which representatives or agents of owners of such marks are prohibited from using such marks, if users are representatives or agents of the mark owners and such use is neither consented to by the mark owners nor justified; (d) Registering or possessing domain names identical with, or confusingly similar to, protected trade names or marks of others, or geographical indications without having the right to use, for the purpose of possessing domain names, benefiting from or prejudicing reputation and popularity of respective marks, trade names or geographical indications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clause 2: 'Commercial indications' include marks, trade names, business symbols, business slogans, geographical indications, designs of packages and/or labels of goods. Clause 3: Acts include affixing such indications on goods/packages/means of service provision/transaction documents/advertising; and selling, advertising, stocking, importing goods affixed with such indications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rights to inventions, industrial designs or layout-designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant for registration knows that such invention or industrial design is being used by another person without prior use right for commercial purposes, the applicant may notify in writing the user of the filing of his/her application, specifying the filing date and the date of application publication so that the user shall terminate or continue such use. If the notified person continues using after grant, the owner shall have the right to request the user to pay compensation equivalent to the price for licensing within the relevant scope and duration of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies also to layout-designs commercially exploited before grant by person with registration right (Clause 2). The right to compensation arises once patent/certificate is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements limiting industrial property rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial property rights may be limited by the following elements: (1) Right of prior users to inventions or industrial designs; (2) Obligations of owners, including payment of remunerations to authors and to use inventions or marks; (3) Licensing of inventions under decisions of state competent agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: State use of inventions for public/non-commercial purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministries and ministerial-level agencies shall have the right, on behalf of the State, to use or permit others to use inventions in domains under their management for public and non-commercial purposes, national defense, security, disease prevention and treatment and nutrition for the people, and other urgent social needs without obtaining permission of invention owners or their licensees, subject to Articles 145 and 146.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use is limited within scope and conditions for licensing provided in Article 146, except where inventions are created using state budget facilities/funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of prior use of inventions and industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who, before the publication date of an application, has used or prepared necessary conditions for use of an invention or industrial design identical with the protected one but created independently (prior use right holder), may continue using such invention/design within the scope and volume of prior use without obtaining permission or paying compensation; such exercise is not an infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior use right is non-assignable except as part of transfer of the business/establishment; prior user must not expand scope/volume unless permitted by owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to pay remunerations to authors (minimum rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners of inventions, industrial designs or layout-designs are obliged to pay remunerations to their authors unless otherwise agreed. Minimum levels: (a) 10% of the profit amount gained by the owner from the use; (b) 15% of total amount received by the owner in each payment for licensing. For co-authors, the remuneration level applies to all co-authors and they shall agree among themselves on division. Obligation exists throughout the term of protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to use inventions and marks (use requirement and consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners of inventions are obliged to manufacture protected products or apply protected processes to satisfy national defense, security, disease prevention and treatment and nutrition needs or other urgent social needs; failure to perform may lead the competent state agency to license such inventions to others without permission. Owners of marks are obliged to use such marks continuously; marks unused for 5 consecutive years or more may have ownership invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use obligations underpin possible compulsory licensing under Articles 145–146.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations re dependent inventions (authorization of principal inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependent invention created based on a principal invention may only be used on condition the principal invention is also used. If the dependent invention offers important technical advance and great economic significance, its owner may request the principal invention owner to license the principal invention on reasonable commercial price and conditions. If the principal owner fails without justifiable reasons, a competent state agency may license the principal invention to the dependent invention owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of assignment of industrial property rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment means transfer of ownership right by owner of such industrial property right to another organization or individual and must be established in written contracts (industrial property right assignment contracts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on assignment of industrial property rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners may only assign rights within the scope of protection. Rights to geographical indications shall not be assigned. Rights to trade names shall only be assigned together with transfer of the entire business establishment and activities under such trade names. Assignment of rights to marks must not cause confusion as to properties or origins of goods or services. Rights to marks shall only be assigned to organizations or individuals who satisfy conditions for persons having the right to register such marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of industrial property right assignment contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment contract must have the following principal contents: (1) Full names and addresses of the assignor and the assignee; (2) Assignment bases; (3) Assignment price; (4) Rights and obligations of the assignor and the assignee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and form of licensing industrial property objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensing means permission by the owner for another to use the industrial property object within the scope of his/her use right. Licensing must be established in written contracts (industrial property object license contracts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions and obligations on licensing industrial property objects
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to use geographical indications or trade names must not be licensed. The right to use collective marks must not be licensed to non-members. The licensee must not enter into a sub-license unless permitted by the licensor. Mark licensees are obliged to indicate on goods and packages that goods have been manufactured under mark license contracts. Invention licensees under exclusive contracts shall be obliged to use such inventions in the same manner as the invention owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of industrial property license contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive contract: licensee has exclusive right to use within scope and term, licensor may neither license others nor use without permission. Non-exclusive contract: licensor retains rights to use and to enter into non-exclusive contracts with others. Industrial property object sub-license contract: contract where the licensor is a licensee under another contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of industrial property object license contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: A license contract must include: (a) Full names and addresses of licensor and licensee; (b) Licensing bases; (c) Contract type; (d) Licensing scope, including use and territorial limitations; (e) Contract term; (f) Licensing price; (g) Rights and obligations of the licensor and the licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited/unreasonable clauses in license contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: License contracts must not have provisions which unreasonably restrict the licensee, particularly: (a) Prohibiting the licensee to improve the industrial property object other than marks; compelling transfer of improvements or rights to improvements free of charge; (b) Directly or indirectly restricting export of goods produced under the license to territories where licensor does not hold rights; (c) Compelling licensee to buy all or certain percentage of inputs from licensor or designee not for quality assurance; (d) Forbidding the licensee to complain about or initiate lawsuits regarding validity of industrial property rights or licensor’s right to license. Any such clauses shall be ex-officio invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for compulsory licensing of inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to use an invention may be licensed to another under a decision of a competent state agency without permission from the holder in cases: (a) Use for public and non-commercial purposes or urgent social needs; (b) Holder fails to fulfill obligations to use within specified durations (4 years from filing / 3 years from grant); (c) Person wishing to use fails to reach agreement despite reasonable negotiation efforts; (d) Holder is considered to have performed anti-competition practices banned by competition law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for compulsory license (scope, exclusivity, assignment, compensation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory licensed use must be non-exclusive; limited to scope and duration sufficient to achieve objectives and largely for domestic market (exceptions for certain cases); licensee must not assign or sub-license except when assignment is with transfer of business establishment; licensee must pay satisfactory compensation depending on economic value and compliant with government compensation bracket. Additional conditions apply for dependent/principal invention relationships: holder of principal invention shall also be licensed to use dependent invention on reasonable terms; licensee of principal must not assign such right except with all rights to dependent invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent authorities and procedures for compulsory licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Science and Technology Ministry issues decisions on licensing for cases b,c,d of Article 145; Ministries and ministerial-level agencies issue decisions for case a after consulting the Science and Technology Ministry. Decisions must set use scope and conditions, promptly notify holders, and may be subject to complaints or lawsuits. Government shall specify procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity and effect of transfer and license contracts upon registration
rubrics_metrics.description: For rights established on registration, an assignment contract is valid upon registration with the state IP agency. An industrial property object license contract is valid as agreed between parties but legally effective to third parties upon registration. Validity of a license contract terminates ex-officio upon termination of licensor’s industrial property rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dossier contents required for registration of transfer contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: A dossier for registration must comprise: (1) A declaration for registration, set form; (2) Original or valid copy of the contract; (3) Original of the protection title for assignment cases; (4) Co-owners’ written consent or explanation for disagreement where rights are jointly owned; (5) Vouchers of payment of fees and charges; (6) Power of attorney if filed through a representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of industrial property representation services
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation services cover: (a) Representing organizations or individuals before competent state agencies in establishment and enforcement of industrial property rights; (b) Providing consultancy on procedures for establishment and enforcement; (c) Other services related to procedures for establishment and enforcement of industrial property rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on representation scope and prohibited acts by representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation organizations shall only provide services within the scope of authorization and may re-authorize others with written consent. They may waive business after transferring incomplete jobs lawfully. Industrial property representatives must not: (a) Concurrently represent parties that dispute over industrial property rights; (b) Withdraw applications, declare waiver of protection or withdraw appeals without consent of authorizing parties; (c) Deceive or force clients to enter into/perform representation service contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities of industrial property representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Representatives must: (a) Clearly notify fee and charge amounts and rates as registered; (b) Keep confidential information and documents; (c) Truthfully and adequately inform all notices and requests of the competent state agency and deliver protection titles and decisions on time; (d) Protect rights and legitimate interests of represented parties by promptly satisfying agency requests in favor of clients; (e) Notify competent agency of changes in names, addresses or other information when necessary. Representation organizations bear civil liabilities for representation performed by their agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for organizations to provide industrial property representation services
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations allowed to provide representation services must: (1) Be law‑practicing businesses or organizations, or scientific and technological service organizations lawfully established and operating; (2) Have the function of providing industrial property representation services stated in their business/operation registration certificates; (3) Have heads or persons authorized by their heads who satisfy the practice conditions specified in Article 155.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and qualifications for individual industrial property representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual is allowed to practice if: (a) Having industrial property representation service-practicing certificate; (b) Working for one representation organization. To be granted a practicing certificate one must: be a Vietnamese citizen with full civil capacity; reside permanently in Vietnam; have a university degree; have 5 consecutive years engaged in IP law domain or examination of registration applications at national/international IP offices or have graduated from recognized IP law training courses; not be cadres/civil servants in the state IP agency; and pass professional examinations. The Government shall specify training, examinations and grant procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording, deletion, and sanctions for representation service organizations and agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations and individuals satisfying conditions shall be recorded in the national register of industrial property representatives and published in the Official Gazette. Where grounds confirm they no longer satisfy conditions, the state agency shall delete their names and publish deletion. Violations of specified provisions by organizations shall be handled according to law. Agents who make professional mistakes or violate provisions may face cautions, monetary fines or withdrawal of practicing certificates depending on nature and seriousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may have rights to plant varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations and individuals who select and breed or discover and develop plant varieties or invest in such activities or are transferred rights may have rights to plant varieties; includes Vietnamese entities, foreign entities under agreements with Vietnam, and foreign entities with permanent residence addresses in Vietnam or establishments producing/trading in plant varieties in Vietnam.

rubrics_metrics.name: General eligibility conditions for plant variety protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant varieties eligible for protection must have been selected and bred or discovered and developed, be on the list of State-protected plant species promulgated by the Agriculture and Rural Development Ministry, and be new, distinct, uniform, stable and designated by proper denominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty requirement and time-limits for plant varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: A plant variety is new if reproductive or harvested materials have not been sold or otherwise distributed for exploitation in Vietnamese territory by the registration right holder or licensee one year before filing; or for exploitation outside Vietnam six years before filing for timber trees or vines, and four years for other plant varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctness requirement for plant varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: A variety is distinct if it is clearly distinguishable from any other variety whose existence is a matter of common knowledge at the time of filing or priority date. Varieties of common knowledge include those widely used in any country's market at filing time, those protected or registered in any country, those subject to protection applications (not rejected), or those whose detailed descriptions have been published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity requirement for plant varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: A plant variety is uniform if, subject to expected variation from propagation characteristics, it is sufficiently uniform in its relevant characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability requirement for plant varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: A plant variety is stable if its originally described relevant characteristics remain unchanged after repeated propagation or, for a propagation cycle, at the end of each cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for denominations of plant varieties (proper and improper denominations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant must designate a proper denomination same as registered in any country upon filing. A proper denomination is distinguishable from those of other varieties of common knowledge in same/similar species. Denominations are improper if (a) numerals only except where relevant to characteristics; (b) violate social ethics; (c) may mislead as to features/characteristics; (d) may mislead as to breeder identification; (e) identical or confusingly similar to marks/trade names/geographical indications protected before publication date; (f) identical or similar to denominations of harvested materials; (g) affect prior rights of others. Those offering reproductive materials for sale must use the denominations as stated in protection titles even after expiration. When combined with trademarks or similar indications, denominations must still be distinguishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of rights to plant varieties (who may register and filing requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain protection, organizations and individuals must file applications with the state management agency in charge. Registrants include breeders who personally selected/bred/discovered/developed varieties; organizations/individuals that fund breeders (job assignment/hiring) unless otherwise agreed; and organizations/individuals transferred or inheriting the right to register for protection.
